takeaway: Drooling from the angle of the mouth after submandibular gland excision means the marginal mandibular branch of the facial nerve was injured, paralysing depressor anguli oris.

lines.text: A 45-year-old man has his submandibular salivary gland removed for sialadenitis.
lines.say: A forty-five-year-old man has his submandibular salivary gland removed for sigh-ah-lad-eh-NIGH-tis.

lines.text: Here the surgeon lifts out the submandibular gland.
The gland was inflamed: that is sialadenitis.
lines.say: The gland was inflamed: that is sigh-ah-lad-eh-NIGH-tis.

lines.text: On the first day after the operation, something is wrong.
He drools saliva from the angle of his mouth, on the side of the operation.
lines.say: He is drooling saliva from the angle of his mouth, on the side of the operation.

lines.text: The nerve at risk is the marginal mandibular branch of the facial nerve.
Injury to it paralyses depressor anguli oris, so saliva escapes from the angle of the mouth.
lines.say: Injury to it paralyzes depressor ang-GYOO-lee OR-iss, so saliva escapes from the angle of the mouth.
